Hykes explained that while Docker's foundational container technology revolutionized environment portability, the tools built around it—like Dockerfiles and Compose—were designed as temporary solutions a decade ago and "frozen in time," inadequately serving today's needs for agent-native developer workflows.

He emphasized that as AI coding agents become more central, environment reproducibility is critical so agents can operate in isolated, portable, and observable environments.

Dagger aims to solve these problems by building an agent-native, modular workflow engine on existing open standards (containers, Git, OpenAI APIs) instead of retrofitting legacy Docker interfaces.

The top row in Custom Mode 1 has Arrangement Record, Set Locator, Previous Locator, and Next Locator from left to right.

Short answer: no. The Launchpad/UG never mentions Live's crossfader or the A/B Crossfade Assign buttons.
Does the Launchpad support cross-fade between A and B for Ableton Live according to the manual?
Session Mode track controls are Record Arm, Mute, Solo, Volume, Pan, Send, Device and Stop Clip (Launchpad/UG/05 Session Mode/04 Track Controls). None of them controls the crossfader.
Does the Launchpad support cross-fade between A and B for Ableton Live according to the manual?
Custom Modes can act as CC faders. Custom 2 ships as eight bipolar horizontal faders on MIDI CC 15–22, which "can be mapped in a DAW" (Launchpad/UG/08 Custom Modes/02 Default Custom Modes).
Does the Launchpad support cross-fade between A and B for Ableton Live according to the manual?

Workaround, not in the Launchpad guide: Live's crossfader maps to any continuous MIDI control (Ableton/Live/UG/18 Mixing/05 Using Live's Crossfader). Use MIDI Map Mode (Ableton/Live/UG/34 MIDI and Key Remote/02 The Mapping Browser/01 Assigning MIDI Remote Control) to map one Custom 2 horizontal fader to the crossfader. Each track's A/B assignment is still set in Live.

Short answer: a pack is how Novation Components handles the Launchpad Pro's sequencer Projects as one set. Get Pack reads the Projects off the device in one go, and the set can be saved to your Novation account or your computer. This comes from a search summary of Novation's Launchpad Pro Mk3 Components guide; the page itself refused automated fetches, so it has not been read word for word.

What goes in it: Projects. A Project stores the sequencer's Patterns, Scenes, scale and root, track types and track MIDI channels, and the device has 64 Project slots (Launchpad/UG/09 Sequencer/12 Projects). The user guide says Components can back up Projects online (Launchpad/UG/09 Sequencer/12 Projects/02 Backup).

User guide for the Launchpad, the Novation Launchpad Pro Mk3 grid controller.
Launchpad Pro is a grid controller for producing and performing with Ableton Live or external MIDI hardware.
Its 64 velocity- and pressure-sensitive RGB pads can launch clips, play notes, and sequence steps. The four-track, 32-step sequencer provides probability and mutation controls for evolving patterns.
Eight Custom Modes can send MIDI to software or hardware. The two MIDI output ports extend control to external instruments.
The unit can operate without a computer when powered through its USB-C port by the included wall adapter.
Ableton Live integration: play, record, and produce from the controller.
Pads: 64 RGB pads sense velocity and pressure.
Sequencer: four tracks with 32-step patterns, scenes, probability, and mutation.
Chord Mode: explore, build, save, and play chords from the grid.
Note and Scale Modes: play melodies and chords in key; Drum Mode maps a drum rack to the grid.
MIDI connections: MIDI In, Out 1, and Out 2/Thru connect external equipment.
Custom Modes: eight editable MIDI layouts made with Novation Components.
Plug in Launchpad Pro to access Novation's Easy Start Tool. It provides setup steps suited to new users and experienced producers, including registration and the included software.
Connect Launchpad Pro to a computer, then open the Easy Start Tool from the device's mounted folder or drive.
Open the LAUNCHPAD folder on the desktop.
Open Click Here to Get Started.html to launch the Easy Start Tool.
If Google Chrome is open when you connect Launchpad Pro, a popup may offer a direct route to Easy Start.

Open Click Here to Get Started.html to launch the Easy Start Tool.
Launchpad Intro offers curated Ampify Music packs for playing loops and one-shots. Its on-screen grid matches the Launchpad Pro pads.
Connect Launchpad Pro to the computer and open Launchpad Intro. The site detects the controller and lets you play the packs.
Launchpad Pro's Session Mode controls Ableton Live's Session View. Live detects the controller when it opens and switches Launchpad Pro to Session Mode.
The guide includes Ableton Live 10 Lite with Launchpad Pro. Novation's Easy Start Tool covers registration, installation, and introductory videos.
Register Launchpad Pro at Novation customer registration to obtain the included license.
Ableton's Learn Live offers further lessons.
Novation Support has setup guidance for other music software.
Session Mode and Note Mode can display different information depending on the software in use.
Power Launchpad Pro from the included wall adapter with the USB-A to USB-C cable.
Connect external hardware with the included TRS minijack-to-DIN adapters and MIDI cables.
Sequencer, Custom, Note, Chord, and Programmer Modes can send MIDI through the MIDI Out ports.
Novation Help Centre provides support and answers to common setup questions.
Shift opens the secondary functions printed on buttons.
Session, Note, Chord, Custom, and Sequencer choose operating modes; Projects opens saved sequencer projects.
The 8×8 pad grid plays notes, launches clips, and edits sequences according to the active mode.
Scene Launch and Sequencer buttons line the grid's right edge; track select and Ableton track controls sit below the grid.
Play and Record/Capture MIDI sit to the left; Setup opens device settings.
USB-C supplies power and connects a computer.
TRS minijacks provide MIDI In, Out 1, and Out 2/Thru.
Session, Note, Chord, Custom, and Sequencer are the five main modes. Press the corresponding button to change the grid's function.
The active mode button glows pale green; available mode buttons glow white.
Projects opens saved sequencer projects and acts as a Sequencer sub-mode.

Custom Mode opens the last used custom layout, initially Custom Mode 1. After pressing Custom, use the track select buttons to choose among eight layouts. The selected layout glows pale green; other available layouts glow dim white.
Novation Components can edit the eight Custom Mode MIDI mappings.
Hold Shift to reach the secondary function printed at the bottom of a button. For example, Save is the shifted function of Projects.
While Shift is held, available functions glow gold and unavailable functions remain unlit.
Shifted toggles such as Record Quantise, Continue, and Click glow red when off and green when on.
Available functions depend on the mode. Save is available in Sequencer Mode.
Session Mode controls Ableton Live Session View from the Launchpad grid. The grid shows an 8 × 8 window of clips.
Session View arranges clips in tracks (columns) and scenes (rows). A clip usually contains looping MIDI or audio. A track hosts an instrument or audio, and a scene launches the clips across its row.
Use the arrow buttons to move the visible 8 × 8 window through the Live set. Live outlines the window currently shown on Launchpad Pro.

Press a clip pad to launch it. Its color matches Live. A queued clip flashes green; a playing clip pulses green. Each track plays one clip at a time, and launching an empty slot stops its playing clip. Use the scene launch buttons at the right to launch a row.
5.1.B — Session View in Live and on the Launchpad grid

For an armed track, Session Record overdubs the playing clip. Shift + Session Record calls Capture MIDI, which retrieves recently played notes from armed or input-monitored tracks into a new clip or overdubs the playing clip.
Play starts the active clips; pressing Play during playback stops playback.
Hold Session while in Session Mode to show a wider map. Each pad represents an 8 × 8 block of clips. Press a pad to jump to its block, or move with the arrow buttons.
The current block is light brown; other blocks are blue. A block with a playing clip outside the current view pulses green.

Session Mode supplies clip selection, editing, quantisation, and recording-length controls.
5.3.1 Select a Clip or Empty Clip Slot
Hold Shift and press a clip or empty slot to select it without launching it. Live focuses that clip and its track. Select an empty slot as the destination when printing from the sequencer.
5.3.1 Select a Clip or Empty Clip Slot
Hold Clear and press a grid pad to delete its clip from Session View. In Note Mode, pressing Clear removes the selected clip.
Hold Duplicate and press a clip pad to copy it into the slot immediately below. An existing clip in that slot is overwritten.
In Note Mode, press Duplicate to copy the selected clip and select the copy for editing.
Double expands a clip to twice its length, such as a two-bar loop becoming four bars.

In Session Mode, hold Shift + Duplicate and press the clip pad. For a selected playing clip in Note or Device Mode, hold Shift and press Duplicate once. In Note Mode, the Double control extends the selected clip for a longer loop or overdub.
Hold Quantise and press a clip pad. Its MIDI notes snap to the nearest sixteenth-note grid point.
Record Quantise snaps newly recorded MIDI to the current quantisation grid.
Hold Shift to inspect the Quantise button: red means off, green means on. While holding Shift, press Quantise to toggle it. In Live, change the grid at Edit → Record Quantisation.
Fixed Length limits new recordings to a chosen number of bars, then stops recording and loops the clip. Press Fixed Length to toggle it: white means off and blue means on.
Briefly hold Fixed Length until the Track Select buttons pulse blue. Press one of those buttons to choose one to eight bars.
The bottom row provides Track Controls for Live. The Track Select buttons immediately above it select the tracks in the current Session View window.
Shows record-arm toggles on the Track Select buttons. Press a track button to arm it for recording; its playing clip stops.
Shows mute toggles on the Track Select buttons. Press a track button to mute it; its playing clip stops.
Shows solo toggles on the Track Select buttons. Press a track button to solo it; its playing clip stops.
Adjust the eight visible tracks with vertical volume faders.
Adjust stereo position with horizontal faders. Rows correspond to tracks, from the leftmost track at the top to the rightmost at the bottom.
Adjust each visible track’s Send A level with a vertical fader.
The row above the mixer selects one of the first eight devices in a track’s chain. After selecting a device, use the eight vertical faders for its macro parameters.
Shows Stop Clip triggers on the Track Select buttons. Press a track button to stop its playing clip at the end of the phrase.
Volume, Send, and Device use vertical faders, with tracks arranged across the grid. Pan uses horizontal faders, with tracks arranged from top to bottom. Press a pad along a fader to set its position.
On an armed track, empty slots glow dim red. Press one to queue recording: the pad and record button flash red. During recording, the pad pulses red and the record button stays bright red.
Press Record to queue the end of recording; the clip flashes red until it stops. Disarming the track stops recording immediately.
Shift gives quick access to Live production commands.
Hold Shift and press Record Arm to undo the last action. Repeat to step back through more actions.
Hold Shift and press Mute to redo an undone action.
Hold Shift and repeatedly press Sends at the desired beat to set Live’s tempo.
Hold Shift and press Solo to toggle Live’s metronome.

Hold a Track Control button to use its view temporarily, then release it to return to the earlier view. For example, hold Volume while viewing Mute, adjust a fader, and release Volume to return to Mute.

Play melodic instruments and drums from the velocity- and pressure-sensitive grid. The layout follows the currently armed Live instrument: a Drum Rack selects Drum Mode, while other instruments use Chromatic or Scale Mode.
Use Up/Down to shift octaves and Left/Right to transpose by semitones. In Live, arm the MIDI track and set monitoring to Auto to hear the instrument.
Note Mode offers Chromatic, Scale, and Drum layouts on an expressive 8 × 8 playing surface. Live automatically changes between Drum and melodic layouts when the armed instrument changes.
Load an instrument or drum kit onto a MIDI track in Live, arm that track, and set its monitor to Auto. Use the arrow buttons to move the playable range.
Chromatic Mode is the default melodic layout and makes every semitone playable. Blue pads are notes in the chosen scale, purple pads are roots, and unlit pads are outside the scale.
With the default five-finger overlap, an octave lies two pads up and two pads right. The sixth column repeats the first column of the row above, allowing guitar-like shapes.
Change the layout in Launchpad/UG/06 Note Mode/04 Note Mode Settings.
Only notes in the chosen scale appear as playable pads. Blue pads mark scale notes, purple marks the root, and unlit pads are beyond the playable range.
Change the layout in Launchpad/UG/06 Note Mode/04 Note Mode Settings.
